investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-11T00:56:54Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production API's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway at the AWS ELB endpoint (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents). Because the failure is shared across all sibling checks with the same error message and zero evidence was collected, the fault is localized to the swarm gateway or the network path between the production API and that ELB, not to any individual check's logic.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service at /v1/agents in us-east-2 that the production API proxies agent provisioning requests to — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST /api/agents call, which in turn requires the swarm gateway to be reachable. Because the gateway returned a connection-level error (not an HTTP 4xx or 5xx from the gateway itself), the production API surfaced a 502 bad_gateway before any agent identity, VM ID, or state could be established, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty. This is an eval-detected infrastructure availability failure scoped to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigation.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 503 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigation.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not been regenerated in 503 minutes, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure entirely to the snapshot freshness assertion and the upstream workflow responsible for publishing it.
investigation.rootCause: The snapshot published at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not been updated for at least 503 minutes. The expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482) requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300. The snapshot's source field reports "desktop-nightly-release", indicating the last successful publish came from a desktop nightly release process rather than a github-actions workflow run. The most likely root cause is that the workflow or process responsible for regenerating and publishing the snapshot file has not executed successfully within the required 5-hour window. This is an eval-layer signal of a stale snapshot artifact; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present to confirm a user-facing outage.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=503, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='desktop-nightly-release', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot is reachable and structurally valid but is 203 minutes past the freshness deadline.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — this is the earliest violated contract boundary.
source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check config shows statusImpact='informational' and required=false, confirming this failure does not itself constitute a required-check outage.
sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed, ruling out a broad website or hosting infrastructure failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2173: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload — the eval correctly measured the live artifact age.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The workflow or automated process responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot (expected to run at least every 300 minutes) did not execute or did not complete successfully within the required window, leaving the previously published artifact in place.

The snapshot source is reported as 'desktop-nightly-release' rather than 'github-actions', suggesting the last successful publish was from a desktop nightly release. If the nightly release cadence is longer than 300 minutes, the snapshot will routinely exceed the freshness contract even without a workflow failure.

A transient or persistent failure in the publish step (e.g., a GitHub Pages deployment failure, a permissions error, or a network issue) may have prevented the updated snapshot from being written to the published URL.

The snapshot generation workflow may have run but produced an artifact with an unchanged or incorrect generatedAt timestamp, causing the computed snapshotAgeMinutes to reflect the prior publish time rather than the current run time.

investigations.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 503 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigations.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not been regenerated in 503 minutes, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure entirely to the snapshot freshness assertion and the upstream workflow responsible for publishing it.
investigations.rootCause: The snapshot published at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not been updated for at least 503 minutes. The expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 482) requires snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300. The snapshot's source field reports "desktop-nightly-release", indicating the last successful publish came from a desktop nightly release process rather than a github-actions workflow run. The most likely root cause is that the workflow or process responsible for regenerating and publishing the snapshot file has not executed successfully within the required 5-hour window. This is an eval-layer signal of a stale snapshot artifact; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present to confirm a user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The workflow or automated process responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot (expected to run at least every 300 minutes) did not execute or did not complete successfully within the required window, leaving the previously published artifact in place.

The snapshot source is reported as 'desktop-nightly-release' rather than 'github-actions', suggesting the last successful publish was from a desktop nightly release. If the nightly release cadence is longer than 300 minutes, the snapshot will routinely exceed the freshness contract even without a workflow failure.

A transient or persistent failure in the publish step (e.g., a GitHub Pages deployment failure, a permissions error, or a network issue) may have prevented the updated snapshot from being written to the published URL.

The snapshot generation workflow may have run but produced an artifact with an unchanged or incorrect generatedAt timestamp, causing the computed snapshotAgeMinutes to reflect the prior publish time rather than the current run time.
